transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

It's too early to say, and you may not need a part at all, because a drain blockage is often just something caught in or behind the pump. Whether you need one, most likely the drain pump, depends on what you find when you check the impeller. From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked pump filter / foreign object in the pump path. With the filter out, shine a torch into the filter opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with a finger. Does it turn freely, was anything caught in it, is it jammed, or do the vanes look broken?
it turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. nothing big caught in it. is that the pump then?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Quite possibly: a stiff, gritty impeller with a clean filter does point towards the drain pump being worn or partly jammed. It isn't certain yet, though, because a blockage further along the drain hose or sump can look the same, so it depends on how the pump behaves when it's actually trying to pump out. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain pump obstructed / jammed or failed. Run a drain or spin-only programme and listen near the bottom front of the machine while it tries to pump out. Does the water pump away, and can you hear the pump humming or is it silent?
the water doesn't pump away. it hums loudly with a bit of a rattle. E18 came up on the display too. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
E18 on your Bosch means: No drainage / drain took too long (clogged coin-trap/pump filter or drain hose). The checks point to the drain pump. I could not find a confirmed match for model FD9409 in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
